A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
caesarean sections reduce the risk of mother to child transmission (MTCT) of HIV by approximately 50%.
we have demonstrated that caesarean delivery can be used as a safe intervention to interrupt mother to child transmission.

the risk of mother to child transmission is reduced by 50% with the use of single-dose nevirapine, and that the risk is reduced by 70% with the use or combination of single-dose zidovudine, single-dose nevaripine and elective caesarean delivery.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the risk of mother to child transmission can be reduced from approximately 25 percent to less than 5 percent with appropriate interventions.
the rate of mother to child transmission (MTCT) is significantly higher when the infant is delivered vaginally than when delivered by caesarean (C-section) section.

, in the absence of antiretroviral therapy (ART), the most effective intervention to prevent mother to child transmission is caesarean delivery, with the greatest effect when the procedure is performed before labour and membrane rupture.
